{"scratch": "d01 Tue 05:40: Looked at nightstand_b1. Found: nothing. Residents: nobody.
- OBSERVATION: Nightstand empty. Resident_1 not in bedroom.
- SCORE ANALYSIS: Score -2.38. Overestimated phone/charger on nightstand (0.45/0.35) while resident was in bathroom. Log(1-p) penalties hurt.
- LESSON: When resident is in Bathroom (morning), mobile electronics (phone/charger) are rarely on nightstand. They are likely ON_PERSON or in Bathroom/Kitchen. Nightstand is for overnight storage, not active morning use.
- ADJUSTMENT: Lower prior for mobile items in bedroom when resident is elsewhere. Focus on static items or 'forgotten' items.

d01 Tue 05:40: Looked at bathroom_shelf_ba1. Found: hairbrush_mara, makeup_kit_mara, medication_bottle_mara. Residents: resident_1.
- OBSERVATION: Static bathroom items confirmed on shelf. Resident present.
- SCORE ANALYSIS: Score -0.86. Above panel average (-1.83). Gained weight (now 0.180, rank 3).
- LESSON: High confidence (0.95) in static items (hairbrush, makeup, meds) on shelf was correct. Low confidence (0.15/0.10) in phone/charger on shelf was likely correct (they were absent). The penalty came from the long tail of 0.01s for 30+ items and the specific misses on phone/charger if they were actually there (but they weren't, so log(1-0.15) is small penalty). Wait, score is log p for present, log(1-p) for absent. Since phone/charger were ABSENT, I got log(1-0.15) and log(1-0.10). These are small negative numbers. The big penalty likely came from the 0.01s for items that were absent? No, log(1-0.01) is very close to 0. The penalty must be from items I assigned high prob to that were absent? I assigned 0.95 to the 3 static items (present, good). I assigned 0.15 to phone (absent, penalty ~-0.16). 0.10 to charger (absent, penalty ~-0.10). The rest are 0.01 or 0.05. log(1-0.05) is ~-0.05. There are ~5 items at 0.05. That's -0.25. Total penalty approx -0.5. Why -0.86? Maybe I missed an item that was there? No, only 3 items found. Maybe the 'everything else left out' implies 0.0? If I left out items, p=0. If an item was absent, log(1-0)=0. If an item was present and I left it out, log(0) = -inf. But I didn't leave out any of the 3 found items. So the score is sum of log(p) for found + log(1-p) for not found. Found: 3 items at 0.95. log(0.95)*3 = -0.153. Not found: phone(0.15), charger(0.10), towel(0.05), water(0.05), glasses(0.05), and ~28 items at 0.01. log(1-0.15)=-0.163. log(1-0.10)=-0.105. log(1-0.05)*3 = -0.157. log(1-0.01)*28 = -0.28. Sum: -0.153 -0.163 -0.105 -0.157 -0.28 = -0.858. Matches -0.86. 
- INSIGHT: My probability distribution was well-calibrated. The score is negative because log probabilities are always negative, but -0.86 is good (close to 0). The main 'cost' is the long tail of 0.01s. To improve, I could lower the tail to 0.005 if I'm confident they are absent, but risk -inf if one is there. Given the static nature of the shelf, 0.01 is a safe floor.
- STRATEGY: Maintain high confidence for static items in their designated spots. Keep low but non-zero confidence for mobile items in static spots. The 'long tail' penalty is unavoidable unless I can confidently exclude items. For bathroom shelf, most items are unlikely, so 0.01 is reasonable.
- CURRENT STATE: Resident in Bathroom. Shelf has static items. Phone/charger likely ON_PERSON or in Kitchen/Entry. Nightstand empty."}
